routeSelection.basis: The Dutch Geschiedenis target uses its general Algemeen graduation direction, the broadest route, rather than a specialized direction or the distinct English History and International Studies trajectory. Second-year choices use the first listed 6-EC course in each period; the third-year extra research seminar uses the first listed alternative. No selection is based on UCR fit.

core: European and world history, empire, modernity and historical argument
Cultural history, public memory, heritage and historical sources
adjacent: War, state power and political conflict, with limited migration-related historical perspectives
Globalisation, capitalism, inequality and environmental change

alternatives.label: History, cultural heritage & public memory
alternatives.concept: A historical core in modern change, gender, empire, war and Indigenous histories leads into cultural heritage, memory and interpretation through art, archaeology, life-writing, historiography and media. The final historical research seminar examines primary sources about Walcheren in 1809. These companion fields do not reproduce VU specialist historical coverage or compulsory individual thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Names the sustained 45 EC dedicated History core and the actual distinct companion disciplines; no specialised migration/economic-history or full external-degree claim.
progression: All 24-course, 180-EC, level-300, PPD, exact semester-availability and hard-prerequisite checks passed. Foundational historical and social inquiry precedes final historical research; contemporary courses are explicitly related applications, not substitutes for period-specific historical modules. The six core History courses run in all alternatives. The research seminar is placed last; course-description-only evidence is identified where the enriched workbook has no outline.

alternatives.label: History, political conflict & social inclusion
alternatives.concept: Historical investigation of empire, warfare and American gender/Indigenous histories leads into rights, political institutions, conflict and social inclusion. Contemporary politics and sociology provide complementary mechanisms and cases; they do not constitute a specialised migration-history sequence. The final historical research seminar works with primary sources about Walcheren in 1809.

alternatives.distinctness: The organising choice materially changes course selection: political theory, institutions, rights, peace/conflict and migrant inclusion replace the extensive art, museum and media-history sequence.

alternatives.label: History, political economy & global inequality
alternatives.concept: The same historical core and source-critical research progression are combined with economic theory, statistical inference and social theory to investigate mechanisms of economic and political change. Economic models and data analysis are complementary tools, not substitutes for economic history or VU History by Numbers. The final historical research is the Walcheren 1809 source project; no historical dataset application in Econometrics is guaranteed.

candidates.label: Historical conflict, rights and social inclusion
Specialist historical crime and genocide enquiry

selection.assessment: Retain three qualified, substantively distinct responses after challenging each from actual content, contribution and weight. Each contains all six available History courses / 45 EC: modern history, American gender history with interviews, empire, warfare, Native American social/cultural history, and a final archival/primary-source research paper on Walcheren 1809. This is sustained historical object/method/progression, not merely a coherent unrelated programme or a generic interest in society. Cultural heritage/public memory adds art/archaeology, historiography, life-writing and historical media; political conflict/social inclusion adds institutions, rights, international relations and sociological enquiry; political economy adds five economic theory/inference courses plus social theory to study mechanisms of historical change. These companions have distinct taught objects/methods and change substantial course weight, not just labels. Their relevance does not make economics, statistics, sociology or contemporary politics into economic/migration history. No UCR composition reproduces VU broader medieval/early-modern and Netherlands sequences, Holocaust-centred genocide historiography, digital-history training, Low Countries devotion research, specialist photography seminar or individual History thesis. Numerical overlap is a feasibility/traceability check, not the comparability argument. Three pass on this basis; no fourth omnibus or generic-method alternative is justified. Two additional candidate directions are explicitly rejected: the illustrative crime-history question (row 4568) does not establish specialist Holocaust/genocide progression in the available UCR courses; migration history (row 4574) has limited support through historical gender/Indigenous inquiry and contemporary inclusion, but lacks a distinct specialist migration-history composition. Their formal registry generator roles remain accounted for through rejected candidates, without authorising another included programme.

notes.text: These are qualified historical responses with cultural, political or economic companions. VU additionally requires specialist medieval/early-modern, Netherlands, Holocaust/genocide, digital-history and regional research work, a current photography-based global seminar and a compulsory individual thesis. UCR statistics and economics do not replace those units; the UCR History Research Seminar concerns Walcheren 1809. Current annual topics and future offerings can change.

audience.programmeDescription: VU History studies Europe and the wider world from antiquity to the present. Students learn to evaluate historical evidence, develop arguments and conduct research through source-based seminars and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three qualified UCR alternatives retain a historical core and a final primary-source research project. They develop cultural heritage and memory, political conflict and social inclusion, or political economy as distinct companion fields. They do not reproduce VU specialist period, regional and digital-history training or its compulsory individual thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC illustration includes two selected Year-2 choices, 30 EC open study, a compulsory 9 EC culture/religion research unit, one selected 9 EC global research seminar, a 3 EC colloquium and a 9 EC thesis. The current selected global seminar studies political photography. Year-3 seminars require all Year 1; thesis and colloquium require all Years 1 and 2. Language testing, attendance, elective-level and approval rules apply; research themes and offerings can change.
